subject: POC bridging: flex-bucket + partial commit proposal
messages:
From: Daniel Cho <daniel@clearbeam.ai>
To: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@clearbeam.ai
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Quick idea to bridge POC runway

Hi Rishi,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team was impressed with the latency profile and the KV caching idea. We wrapped up our internal review and have a short runway problem: we need another 3–4 weeks to finish integration tests, but our quarter budget for evaluation credits has already been committed.

Instead of a straight extension, would Redwood consider a short bridging offer that mixes a smaller timebox extension with a reduced committed bucket? For example: a four-week bridge with a small partial commit we can convert to credit on purchase. That keeps momentum without forcing a full-blown contract right away.

Key asks from our side:
- 3–4 week extension or equivalent credits
- Option to convert those credits to committed capacity if we sign within 60 days
- Clarity on data retention and logs during the extension for compliance review

Attached is a summary of our internal timeline (Proposed-MAP-2027.xlsx). Procurement is copied. If you can sketch numbers, I can take to finance tomorrow.

Best,
Daniel
Director of ML Infrastructure
Clearbeam Analytics

---
Attachments: Proposed-MAP-2027.xlsx (spreadsheet)
From: rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Daniel Cho <daniel@clearbeam.ai>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai, procurement@clearbeam.ai
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2027 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Quick idea to bridge POC runway

Daniel — really appreciate the clear asks and the timeline. We can do a bridging structure that aligns incentives and keeps the POC moving. High-level options (pick one):

1) Flex-bucket bridge (recommended)
- 4-week term, preloaded with 50k token-equivalent credits (usable across generation & embeddings)
- If you convert to a 3-month committed package within 60 days, 100% of bridge credits convert to committed credit plus a 5% one-time conversion discount
- No SLA change during bridge; standard hosted API terms apply
- Price: $7,500 for the 4-week bucket (net after early-conversion discount if exercised)

2) Timebox extension + partial commit
- 4-week timeboxed extension + 6-month minimum partial commit (mid-tier) with 8% discount on committed monthly spend
- Upfront invoice covers one week of extension + one month of partial commit; remainder billed monthly
- Price will vary with committed scale; I can model if you share expected QPS / avg tokens

3) Credit-only top-up (fastest)
- One-off credit top-up: 30k tokens for $4,800. Non-convertible.

Security/compliance notes:
- During bridge we will retain request logs for 90 days unless you request extended retention (we can arrange 12 months on dedicated/private deployments)
- Point-of-contact for security: laura_bennett@redwood.ai (copying Laura)

I've attached a short one-pager (Flex-Bucket-Offer-CLB.pdf) that outlines the flex-bucket option and the conversion mechanics. If procurement prefers, we can route a short addendum through DocuSign that captures the bridge terms only.

Let me know which option you want to move forward with — I can get a formal addendum ready today.

Thanks,
Rishi Malhotra
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0199

---
Attachments: Flex-Bucket-Offer-CLB.pdf (PDF summary)
From: Daniel Cho <daniel@clearbeam.ai>

Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2027 14:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Quick idea to bridge POC runway

Rishi — thanks, this is exactly the shape we had in mind. A few clarifying questions before procurement can greenlight: 

- For the flex-bucket: can you reduce the minimum to 40k tokens and keep the 60-day conversion window? Our usage estimate is quite spiky so we want to avoid over-commit.
- If we convert, will the conversion discount be applied to committed monthly spend or as a one-time rebate credit? We prefer committed spend reduction.
- Can you confirm there is no additional data export fee for producing the request logs we need for the SOC review?

Procurement also asked about invoice timing and whether DocuSign must precede the first invoice. If we accept the flex-bucket, procurement prefers an invoice after the DocuSign addendum is signed.

If you can confirm those points, I will route to finance and come back with a PO by EOD tomorrow.

—Daniel

From: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Daniel Cho <daniel@clearbeam.ai>
Cc: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, procurement@clearbeam.ai
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2027 16:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Quick idea to bridge POC runway

Hi Daniel — copying in sales ops and CS to address the operational points. Quick answers: 

- We can accept 40k tokens for the flex-bucket.
- Conversion discount mechanics: we apply a one-time credit equal to 5% of the bridge spend that posts as a credit on your first committed invoice; if you prefer we can apply to committed monthly rate, we will need to confirm with billing but that is feasible. Say which you prefer and we'll lock it in.
- No charge for exporting request logs for SOC-related review; we'll provide the export as an S3 share. Standard export SLAs apply (24–48 hours).
- DocuSign: we will generate a 1-page addendum. Procurement signature before invoice is standard — we'll wait for signed DocuSign before charging.

Marissa (Customer Success) will schedule a quick kickoff to confirm integration points once the addendum is signed.

Thanks,
Laura Bennett
Head of Sales Operations | Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwood.ai
